Publication-quality feature plot

Source: R/feature_plots.R
FeaturePlot_bioToolkit.Rd

Colours cells on a 2D reduction (UMAP, tSNE, PCA, ...) by the values of one or more features (genes, metadata columns, module scores, ...). Like DimPlot_bioToolkit, every panel has a fixed absolute size set by `panel.width` and `panel.height`, so that panels are identical across figures; use save_plot to save the plot, or a patchwork combination of plots, sized to fit. Text sizes follow theme_bioToolkit, and the values behind each panel can be written out with export_source_data.

Cells go through three steps:

  1. `cells` selects the cells that are plotted at all; the others are left out entirely.

  2. `split.by` divides the plotted cells into panels.

  3. Within each panel, cells that are in `cells.highlight` and have a value above `na.cutoff` are coloured by their value. All other plotted cells are drawn beneath them in `na.value` grey, which is never shown in the legend and does not affect the colour scale.

Values can be shown per cell (`geom = "point"`), averaged into hexagonal tiles (`geom = "hex"`), or smoothed over neighbouring cells (`geom = "density"`), which recovers the signal of sparse genes.

Usage

FeaturePlot_bioToolkit(
  object,
  features,
  cells = NULL,
  cells.highlight = NULL,
  full.extent = FALSE,
  split.by = NULL,
  keep.scale = "feature",
  reduction = "umap",
  dims = c(1, 2),
  assay = NULL,
  slot = "data",
  geom = c("point", "hex", "density"),
  cols = NULL,
  na.value = NULL,
  na.cutoff = "auto",
  min.cutoff = NA,
  max.cutoff = NA,
  diverging = "auto",
  center = 0,
  order = TRUE,
  pt.size = 0.3,
  alpha = 1,
  outline = FALSE,
  outline.color = "black",
  outline.size = 0.6,
  label = FALSE,
  label.by = NULL,
  label.size = 3.5,
  label.color = "black",
  hex.bins = 60,
  hex.fun = c("mean", "pct"),
  hex.min.cells = 3,
  density.method = c("smooth", "wkde"),
  density.adjust = 1,
  legend.position = c("right", "left", "top", "bottom", "inside", "none"),
  legend.direction = NULL,
  legend.title = "auto",
  legend.title.face = "auto",
  legend.length = 1.5,
  legend.width = 0.15,
  legend.text.size = NULL,
  ncol = NULL,
  by.row = TRUE,
  arrow.panels = c("bottom.left", "all", "left", "right", "top", "bottom", "none"),
  combine = TRUE,
  panel.width = 4,
  panel.height = panel.width,
  panel.spacing = 0.1,
  strip.text.size = NULL,
  strip.text.face = "bold",
  raster = NULL,
  raster.threshold = 10000,
  raster.dpi = 1000,
  bg = "transparent",
  seed = 42,
  ...
)

Arguments

object

A Seurat object

features

Features to plot: genes, metadata columns or anything else Seurat::FetchData() accepts. Several features are drawn as one panel each, and only one feature can be given with `split.by`

cells

Cells to plot, as names or indices (e.g. from Seurat::WhichCells()). Other cells are left out of the plot entirely. If NULL (default), all cells are plotted

cells.highlight

Cells to colour, as names or indices. Other plotted cells are drawn in `na.value`. If NULL (default), all plotted cells can be coloured

full.extent

Whether the axes span all cells of the object rather than only the plotted ones, so that a plot of a subset of cells lines up with a plot of the whole object. Default is FALSE

split.by

Metadata column to split the plot by, one panel per level. If NULL (default), a single panel per feature is drawn

keep.scale

How colour scales are shared between panels, as in Seurat::FeaturePlot(): "feature" (default) gives all panels of a feature one scale and one legend; "all" gives every panel of every feature one scale; NULL gives each panel its own scale and legend

reduction

Name of the reduction to plot, default is "umap"

dims

The two dimensions of the reduction to plot, default is 1 and 2

assay

Assay that genes are read from. If NULL (default), the default assay of the object (SeuratObject::DefaultAssay()), as in Seurat. The assay and layer used are reported in a message. Genes are fetched from this assay only: a gene that is only in another assay is an error rather than being read from it silently. Objects holding both "RNA" and "SCT" assays give different values for the same gene, so set it explicitly for reproducible figures

slot

Layer to fetch expression from, default is "data"

geom

How values are drawn: "point" (default) colours each cell; "hex" colours hexagonal tiles by a summary of the cells in them (see `hex.fun`); "density" colours each cell by values smoothed over neighbouring cells (see `density.method`)

cols

The colours of the scale. If NULL (default), "plasma_r" or, for a diverging scale, "blue-magenta". Otherwise two or more colours from low to high values, e.g. `c("grey90", "darkred")` (low, high) or, for a diverging scale, `c("#2166AC", "white", "#B2182B")` (low, centre, high); or the name of a sequential or diverging palette (see show_palettes), such as "viridis", "magma" or "tol-burd", or of an RColorBrewer palette

na.value

Colour of cells (or tiles) that are not coloured. If NULL (default), "grey88", or "grey70" for a diverging scale so that they stand out from its light centre

na.cutoff

Values at or below this are drawn in `na.value` rather than on the colour scale. "auto" (default) uses 0 for features with no negative values, so that cells with no expression are told apart from cells with low expression, and no cutoff otherwise, and for `geom = "density"`. NULL plots all values on the colour scale

min.cutoff, max.cutoff

Lower and upper ends of the colour scale, one per feature or a single value for all. Values beyond them get the colour of the end. A number sets the end exactly, so that separate plots share colours; a quantile such as "q1" or "q99" is computed from the coloured values; NA (default) uses the smallest or largest value

diverging

Whether to use a diverging scale centred on `center`: "auto" (default) does so when the coloured values span `center`, or TRUE / FALSE

center

Centre of a diverging scale, default is 0. The two sides of the scale extend equally far in colour from the centre, so that a side with a smaller range does not reach its darkest colour

order

Whether to draw cells with higher values on top, default is TRUE; on a diverging scale, cells further from the centre are drawn on top. If FALSE, cells are drawn in random order

pt.size

Point size, default is 0.3

alpha

Point (or tile) transparency, default is 1

outline

Whether to draw an outline around the cell clouds, default is FALSE. Not used for `geom = "hex"`

outline.color

Colour of the outline, default is "black"

outline.size

Thickness of the outline (in point size units), default is 0.6

label

Whether to label groups at their median position, default is FALSE. Groups are the active identities unless `label.by` is given

label.by

Metadata column whose groups are labelled when `label = TRUE`. If NULL (default), the active identities

label.size

Size of the group labels in mm, default is 3.5

label.color

Colour of the group labels, default is "black"

hex.bins

Number of hexagons across the width of a panel, default is 60. Hexagons are regular for any panel shape

hex.fun

Summary of a tile: "mean" (default) is the mean value of its coloured-eligible cells, counting those at or below `na.cutoff`; "pct" is the percentage of them above `na.cutoff` (or 0 when there is none). Tiles with no such cell, or a summary at or below the cutoff, are drawn in `na.value`

hex.min.cells

Tiles with fewer plotted cells are not drawn, default is 3

density.method

For `geom = "density"`: "smooth" (default) is a kernel-weighted mean of the values of neighbouring cells, which keeps the units of the feature and is comparable between panels; "wkde" is a kernel density of cells weighted by their values, as in the Nebulosa package, scaled to a maximum of 1 per feature. It is highest where many cells have high values, and needs non-negative values

density.adjust

Multiplier of the smoothing bandwidth, default is 1. Smaller values smooth less

legend.position

Position of the legend, one of "right" (default), "left", "top", "bottom", "inside" or "none"

legend.direction

Direction of the colour bar, "vertical" or "horizontal". If NULL (default), horizontal for top and bottom legends and vertical otherwise

legend.title

Title of the colour bar: "auto" (default) for the feature name (or "Expression" / "Value" for a scale shared by several features); NULL for no title; or a string, or one string per feature (optionally named by feature)

legend.title.face

Font face of the legend title. "auto" (default) sets it in bold, gene names in bold italics

legend.length

Length of the colour bar in inches, default is 1.5

legend.width

Thickness of the colour bar in inches, default is 0.15

legend.text.size

Font size of the legend text and title in points. If NULL (default), the theme's base size (11)

ncol

Number of panel columns. If NULL (default), split panels are laid out in a single row, and several features in up to four columns as in Seurat::FeaturePlot()

by.row

Whether panels fill the grid row by row (default, TRUE) or column by column (FALSE)

arrow.panels

Panels that get the dimension arrows: "bottom.left" (default; the first panel of the bottom row), "all", "left" / "right" (the first / last panel of each row), "top" / "bottom" (the top / lowest panel of each column) or "none". With `combine = FALSE`, every plot gets its own arrows unless "none"

combine

Whether to return a single plot (default, TRUE) or a list of one plot per panel, each with its own arrows, to be arranged by the caller

panel.width

Width of a single panel in inches, default is 4

panel.height

Height of a single panel in inches, default is `panel.width`

panel.spacing

Gap between panels in inches, default is 0.1

strip.text.size

Font size of the panel labels in points. If NULL (default), the theme's large size (12)

strip.text.face

Font face of the panel labels, default is "bold". Gene names are additionally set in italics

raster

Whether to rasterize the points while keeping text, legend and arrows as vectors: NULL (default) rasterizes when there are more than `raster.threshold` cells, or TRUE / FALSE. Hex tiles are always drawn as vectors

raster.threshold

Number of cells above which `raster = NULL` rasterizes, default is 10000

raster.dpi

Resolution of the rasterized points, default is 1000. Match the `dpi` used when saving raster (e.g. png) output

bg

Background colour, default is "transparent", so that the figure can be placed on any background (gaps inside outlines and label halos are then white). Use e.g. "white" for an opaque background

seed

Random seed used for drawing order and label placement, default is 42. The global random number generator state is not changed

...

Arguments of the dimension arrows, as in add_dimension_arrows: the arrows scale with the panel size, and `arrow.scale` makes them larger or smaller (e.g. `arrow.scale = 0.8`; default 1, 2 cm arrows on a 3.5-inch panel); the snake_case names used before 0.10.0 are deprecated

Value

A ggplot object when there is a single colour scale over one feature; otherwise a patchwork object, whose panels keep their fixed size when combined further with patchwork. With `combine = FALSE`, a named list of ggplot objects
